ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are three squares respectively connected to the three sides of a right triangle. The square on the left is labeled 16, the smaller square at the bottom is labeled 9, and the tilted square at the upper right is labeled A; the figure also marks the right angle, indicating that the triangle sides corresponding to the two squares labeled 16 and 9 are the legs. Reasoning: The side length of the square with area 16 is sqrt(16)=4, and the side length of the square with area 9 is sqrt(9)=3. These two sides are the two legs of the right triangle, so the square of the hypotenuse length is 4^2+3^2=16+9=25. Square A is built on the hypotenuse, and its area is equal to the square of the hypotenuse length, therefore the area of A is 25.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: three squares are attached to the three sides of a right triangle; the left square is labeled 16, the bottom square is labeled 9, and the tilted square on the slanted side is labeled A. From the text, take 16 and 9 as the areas of the two smaller squares. Convert these areas to side lengths: the corresponding triangle legs have lengths sqrt(16)=4 and sqrt(9)=3. Since the image shows these two sides meet at a right angle, use the Pythagorean theorem to find the slanted side length squared: 4^2+3^2=16+9=25. The area of the square on that slanted side is therefore 25.
